subject: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@medicahealth.com>; Procurement <procurement@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks

Hi Elena / Medica procurement team —

Thanks for the quick conversation yesterday. Per our call, I pulled together a short heatmap and a proposed Mutual Action Plan that reflects your tightened acceptance window (the evaluation window is now 7 business days rather than the 3-week window we originally planned). Attached: MAP_MedicaHealth_v2.xlsx and EvaluationPlan_v1.md.

Summary / immediate asks (high priority):
- Acceptance window: target firm go-live candidate week is 2026-10-18. That gives us a 7-business-day functional evaluation window: 2026-10-18 -> 2026-10-26.
- Procurement: to preserve that window we need a signed PO or a DocuSign-signed SOW by end-of-day 2026-10-06. Any delay beyond 2026-10-06 will force us into the fallback cadence below.
- Technical gating: we must confirm VPN/WireGuard access to the test VPC by 2026-10-11 or the evaluation cannot complete in time.
- Risk heatmap (high level):
  * Procurement lag — high impact, high likelihood (Procurement holds legal sign-off until 10/12)
  * Environment readiness — medium impact (delayed test credentials)
  * Evaluation scope creep — medium impact

Proposed mitigations in the MAP:
1) Shortened acceptance checklist (critical 8 items) — see tab "Critical Check" in MAP_MedicaHealth_v2.xlsx.
2) Parallel legal redline sprint — Rishi to coordinate 2x 30-min lock-step sessions with Medica legal on 10/02 & 10/04.
3) Exec-level approval path — if PO misses 10/06, request a one-off credit to preserve test window; Redwood execs to review on 10/07.

If you confirm procurement timing and VPN readiness, we'll lock the evaluation itinerary and reserve the cluster. If procurement cannot hit 10/06, please tell us which of these three options you prefer: (A) shift evaluation by two weeks; (B) accept a reduced test scope (4 days); (C) sign a temporary MOU to permit testing while SOW completes.

Thanks — sending this per our internal risk log and stepping up to exec if needed.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: MAP_MedicaHealth_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), EvaluationPlan_v1.md (markdown), SOW_redlines_v1.pdf (redlines)

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@medicahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicahealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T12:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks

Olga —

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP draft. A few quick notes from procurement and program management:

- Procurement: current internal timeline has legal sign-off earliest 10/12 (we have a backlog for the vendor legal queue). PO by 10/06 is unlikely unless we escalate. I’ve looped procurement and asked for a priority review (they're on copy).
- VPN/test VPC: IT confirmed they can provide test endpoints by 10/13, not 10/11.
- Evaluation scope: ClinOps will not accept less than a representative 5-day functional run for regulatory sampling.

Given those constraints, our preferred option is (C) — sign an MOU / temporary access agreement so testing can proceed while legal finalizes the SOW. Procurement asked what an acceptable MOU would look like from Redwood.

Elena
Elena Gomez
Director, Product & Clinical Programs | MedicaHealth
elena.gomez@medicahealth.com | (617) 555-4281

On Sep 30, 2026, at 09:12 AM PDT, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message attached)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks

Team — quick internal note after Elena's reply:

- Procurement unwilling to commit to 10/06 for PO; MOU path is feasible. We should draft a minimal MOU that covers: scope for the test, data handling boundaries, and temporary access terms. Legal will need to sign off but that is usually faster than full SOW review.
- If IT's earliest test endpoints are 10/13 and ClinOps requires 5 days, the latest safe go/no-go tick is 10/20 (end of functional run). That pushes our original go-live candidate by ~2 weeks if we keep validation integrity.
- Mitigation plan (working draft):
  1) Draft MOU by 10/01 EOD — Rishi
  2) Escalate to Redwood ops for reserved window between 10/18-10/25 and confirm cluster hold — Mina
  3) Prep a reduced-scope test script (5-day) that still satisfies ClinOps sampling — Camila

I'll own the consolidated risk log and will produce a 1-page executive readout if we need to route a credit/exception ask.

Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Product Manager | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@medicahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks

Elena — thanks for the quick context. We can absolutely do an MOU template to bridge testing while legal finishes the SOW. Short answers to the asks: 

- MOU content: we propose a 1-page MOU limited to: (1) permission to access Medica test data sandbox, (2) statement of limited liability for testing activities, (3) retention/erase commitment for test artifacts, and (4) a mutual termination clause tied to SOW execution. Draft attached: SOW_redlines_v1.pdf (contains suggested MOU language at the front).
- Timeline: I will circulate a one-page MOU by 2026-10-01T16:00 (ET) and request procurement attach a priority ticket. If Medica can sign the MOU by 2026-10-04 we can keep the 10/18 evaluation start with a 5-day run concluding 10/22.
- Exec ask: if procurement cannot sign the MOU by 10/04, we will need an exception for cluster reservation fees. Camila — please confirm the reserve hold cost so I can include it in the executive note.

Action items (owner / due):
- Rishi: circulate one-page MOU -> 2026-10-01 16:00 ET (in flight)
- Camila: reserve cluster & confirm cost -> 2026-10-01 EOD PT
- Mina: prepare escalation note and the credit/exception template -> 2026-10-02

Thanks — I will follow up with procurement directly if needed.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@medicahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Compressed acceptance window: heatmap, risks, and urgent approval asks

Elena / team — final confirmation and escalation path.

- We have reserved an evaluation cluster tentatively for 10/18–10/25 (pending MOU). Hold cost for the reserved cluster is $1,800 for the reserved week. If Medica signs MOU by 10/04 we will waive the hold fee; otherwise, we will invoice the hold fee (or apply to credits against a delayed go-live).
- If procurement cannot sign the MOU by 10/04 and cannot accept the hold fee, we will need an exec approval for a one-time credit to keep the scheduling intact. I'll escalate to our Head of Sales on 10/05 if we don't have MOU/PO confirmation.

Next steps:
- Rishi circulate MOU (in flight)
- Elena / procurement: confirm MOU path or inform which option (A/B/C) you prefer by 2026-10-02
- Camila: reduced-scope script draft by 2026-10-02

If we have to shift the evaluation window, we recommend 10/31–11/06 (two-week push) to preserve 5 business days of testing plus buffer.

Thanks all,

Mina Haddad
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: ProcurementChecklist_Medica.pdf
